label: fix

issues.concern: Duration-of-protection promise (repeated as '8 HOURS+ SPF PROTECTION') has no recognised SPF test method behind it and undercuts reapplication advice (brand_corpus §3.6); risks under-protection (ASCI-3.3, ASCI-1.1) in ASCI's current SPF enforcement focus (ASCI-RPT-HEAT). Remove or route to legal (Q4).

issues.phrase: helps you to get clear and acne free skin
issues.concern: Acne-elimination outcome on a sunscreen (repeated as 'acne & oil free skin') moves past the audience descriptor toward mitigation (DCA-DRUG-DEF; open Q1, route to legal); ingredient benefits sold as product efficacy (ASCI-RPT-BPC); 'you' + acne implies a health attribute (META-PA).
Conflicts with 'SPF 50' in the headline; the stated SPF must match the label and the in-vivo report on file (BIS-SPF, ASCI-1.1; Q4).
Test claim needs lab/study source and date in the ad (ASCI-1.2) and an IS 17494 / ISO 24444 report on file (BIS-SPF; open Q4).
Unsubstantiated superlative/superiority claim (ASCI-1.1; ASCI-RPT-BPC leadership claims; ASCI-G-AWARD: superiority needs research).
Implies other formulas are toxic - vague, misleading safety claim (COS-R36) and the chemophobic fear framing Minimalist explicitly rejects (brand_corpus §6, S3).

Free-from framing denigrates legally permitted UV filters (EU-655-4/5/6 §5(1); open Q12) and would disparage Minimalist's own Light Fluid SPF, whose page (S6) names ethylhexyl methoxycinnamate, i.e. OMC (brand_corpus §5); also misspelled.
Hype vocabulary absent from Minimalist copy ('revolutionary' = 0, brand_corpus §4.1); conflicts with 'No unnecessary marketing fluff' (§6).

issues.phrase: highest-quality ingredients which is backed by advanced science
issues.concern: 'Backed by science' carries legal weight and ingredient literature is not product proof (CCPA-4 4(1)(b),(f)); 'highest-quality' is puffery.

issues.phrase: suitable for anyone with sensitive skin
issues.concern: Universal suitability; soften to 'suitable for sensitive skin' with patch-test data on file (ASCI-1.1; EU-655-4/5/6 rewrite).

reviewer_note: No hard drug or fairness claim, but the 8-hour protection promise, acne-free outcome, SPF 50 vs 50+ mismatch and 'thinnest' superlative must be fixed or substantiated before this sunscreen copy runs.

label: fix

issues.concern: Structure/function claim - DMR-2's own example ('Boosts collagen production'); open Q2, route to legal; rewrite e.g. 'helps skin look firmer'.

Reads as 20% collagen content, yet no collagen appears among the listed actives; a % tied to a benefit is misleading by ambiguity (ASCI-1.4; CPA-2(28)) and breaks concentration transparency (brand_corpus §6; open Q5).
Percentage attached to a benefit, not an ingredient - can read as an 18% brightening result (ASCI-1.4; ASCI-RPT-BPC 'Y% more' with unclear basis); name the actives (11% + 5% + 2%) instead.
Name the actual ingredient (e.g. mandarin extract, per INCI); Minimalist names the molecule with its % (brand_corpus §2.1).

reviewer_note: Ingredient-led naming is on-brand, but 'Collagen Boost' (Q2) and percentages pinned to benefits rather than named ingredients must be reworked before it runs.

label: block

issues.concern: Positions a cosmetic 'for' named medical conditions (rosacea, cystic acne) plus a pharmacological action - drug language (DCA-DRUG-DEF lists rosacea; CDSCO-PN-2026 on 'treatment' positioning; ASCI-3.4; cf. ASCI-G-INF-HEALTH 'treats cystic acne' example).
Antibacterial mitigation claim on acne (DCA-DRUG-DEF; open Q1/Q2 - route to legal).
Structure/function verb named in open Q2 ('regulates sebum'); route to legal; e.g. 'helps control the look of oil'.

issues.phrase: reduces the formation of open pores (or blackheads)
issues.concern: Scientifically inaccurate structure claim (blackheads are not open pores) (Q2; COS-R36) - wrong for a science-first brand (brand_corpus §6).

issues.phrase: this mineral is loved for its anti-inflammatory, antibacterial and mattifying properties
issues.concern: Wrong ingredient fact: witch hazel is a plant extract, not a mineral, and 'It essential for healthy skin' is untrue (COS-R36, CPA-2(28)); repeats drug-like anti-inflammatory/antibacterial claims (Q2).
'Clean/non-toxic' implies other products are toxic - misleading (COS-R36) and the chemophobic framing Minimalist rejects (brand_corpus §6, S3).
Fear framing that standard ingredients are toxic to skin (brand_corpus §6 'fear mongering'; EU-655-4/5/6 §5(1) on denigrating legal ingredients).
Natural-origin claim - keep supplier proof on file (ASCI-RPT-BPC natural claims); natural halo sits badly with brand_corpus §6 anti-'natural' stance.

reviewer_note: Positioning a cosmetic serum for rosacea and cystic acne with anti-inflammatory/antibacterial claims is drug territory Minimalist cannot publish, on top of factual errors and 'non-toxic' fear framing.

label: fix

issues.concern: Concentration conflict: headline '8%' reads as 8% glycolic, but the body twice says '1% Glycolic Acid' with '2% Niacinamide' and never quantifies Melasyl - misleading on quantity (ASCI-1.4; CPA-2(28)); reconcile with the formula (brand_corpus §6 concentration transparency).

issues.phrase: helps fade dark spots in as little as 4 weeks
issues.concern: Time-bound result needs a finished-product study on file and a qualifier/source (ASCI-1.1, ASCI-1.2; META-HW-CLAIMS timeframe promises).

issues.phrase: reduces dullness and excess melanin appearance
issues.concern: Melanin wording is a drug claim in the US (FDA-DEF) and depigmentation phrasing is open Q3; keep to 'the look of dark spots'.

issues.phrase: apply 2-3 drops evenly across the face
issues.concern: Daily AHA directions omit daytime sunscreen; add SPF guidance (ASCI-3.3; Minimalist's own copy: 'Use sunscreen during the day', brand_corpus §4.2).

reviewer_note: Mostly hedged, cosmetic-safe copy, but the headline '8%' conflicts with the 1% glycolic / 2% niacinamide stated in the body and the 4-week result needs a study and qualifier.

label: fix

issues.phrase: Visibly Reduces Dark Spots from Day 7
issues.concern: Time-bound result with no qualifier or study reference (META-HW-CLAIMS; ASCI-1.1); the fast-result pattern ASCI-RPT-HEAT flagged ('Visible Difference in 5 Days').

issues.phrase: leaving skin radiant, glowing and clear from the very first week
issues.concern: Exaggerated fast-transformation promise (ASCI-1.5; ASCI-RPT-HEAT).
Testing claim needs source and date in the ad (ASCI-1.2; open Q8); 'dermatologically tested' in the body is open Q6.

Safety absolute on a 10% glycolic acid serum used nightly; soften to 'suitable for most skin types; patch test' with data on file (ASCI-1.5, ASCI-3.3; cf. Minimalist's acid cautions, brand_corpus §3.7).
Organic claim needs certification on file; an organic halo on a largely synthetic acid serum is an ASCI enforcement pattern (ASCI-RPT-BPC).

issues.phrase: preserves active principles of Turmeric to visibly reduce dark spots
issues.concern: Ingredient efficacy presented as product efficacy (ASCI-RPT-BPC; Q5).

issues.phrase: Free from mineral oils, parabens, phthalates, silicones, SLS and SLES
issues.concern: Free-from list implies legal ingredients are harmful (EU-655-4/5/6 §5(1); open Q12); at odds with brand_corpus §6 anti-fear stance.

reviewer_note: No drug or fairness claim, but the Day-7 / first-week results, unsourced 'Clinically Tested', organic halo and 'safe for all skin types' on a 10% AHA all need fixing or evidence.

label: fix

issues.concern: Comparative stats with no stated basis (vs what, measured how?) - ASCI-RPT-BPC 'Y% more' pattern; ASCI-4.1; ASCI-G-DISC requires the basis of comparison.
Duration claim needs a finished-product hydration study on file, cited in the ad (ASCI-1.1, ASCI-1.2).
'Approved' implies expert endorsement; needs a test report and legal view (ASCI-RPT-BPC expert recommendation; open Q6).
'Instant' is hype Minimalist never uses (brand_corpus §4.1) and an ASCI-RPT-HEAT watch term; acceptable only as a tested sensory claim.
'100% natural' framing is what Minimalist's philosophy criticises (brand_corpus §6, S3); keep the ingredient spec on file.

reviewer_note: Benign moisturiser copy undermined by unexplained '2X / 300%' comparisons, an uncited 72-hour claim and 'dermatologically approved'.

label: fix

issues.phrase: clinically proven to brighten skin in 5 days
issues.concern: 'Clinically proven' with no source/date (ASCI-1.2; Q8) plus a 5-day result - the exact pattern ASCI-RPT-HEAT flagged ('Visible Difference in 5 Days').

Whole face-and-body brightening led by glutathione (commonly marketed for skin lightening) reads as skin-lightening - ASCI-G-FAIR / META-HW-WHITEN exposure; open Q3, route to legal; reframe to radiance or the look of dullness.
Unqualified multiplier with no basis (ASCI-RPT-BPC '30X' pattern; ASCI-4.1); an ingredient comparison is not product proof (CCPA-4 4(1)(f)).

issues.phrase: Dewy glowing skin from first use
issues.concern: Instant-result promise (ASCI-1.5; ASCI-RPT-HEAT instant transformation; META-HW-CLAIMS timeframe).

issues.phrase: Provides 48 hours of glowing radiant skin
issues.concern: Duration claim for a visual outcome needs a study and qualifier (ASCI-1.1, ASCI-1.2).
Stat with no baseline, sample or method (ASCI-1.1, ASCI-1.2; ASCI-RPT-BPC).
Multiplier with no basis instead of a stated % (ASCI-RPT-BPC; brand_corpus §6 concentration transparency).
Precise time claim needs test data on file (ASCI-1.1).
Unclear, likely unsubstantiable penetration claim - misleading by ambiguity (ASCI-1.4); structure-type language (Q2).

reviewer_note: A stack of unsourced multipliers, fast-result and 'clinically proven' claims plus glutathione-led 'brighter skin' - runnable only after studies are on file and legal clears the brightening framing.

issues.concern: Repair/heal language beyond the cosmetic definition (DCA-COS-DEF 'Heals damaged skin barrier' example); open Q2 - route to legal; e.g. 'helps support the skin barrier'.
Duration claim needs a finished-product hydration study on file, cited in the ad (ASCI-1.1, ASCI-1.2).

Ambiguous fragrance claim contradicted by the body ('Features a pleasant almond scent'); state 'no added fragrance' or drop the fragrance-free claim (ASCI-1.4, COS-R36) - matters on a sensitive-skin product.
Absolute 'prevents'; prefer 'helps reduce moisture loss' backed by TEWL data.

issues.phrase: Target Audience: Suitable for both men and women
issues.concern: Marketplace/SEO scaffolding labels ('Target Audience:', 'Brand and Product:') are not ad copy.

reviewer_note: Plain spec-style copy, but 'Repairs Skin' (Q2), an uncited 48H claim and the fragrance-free vs almond-scent contradiction need fixing first.

issues.phrase: Clinically proven to provide continuous hydration
issues.concern: 'Clinically proven' with no source/date in the ad (ASCI-1.2; CCPA-12 12(b); open Q8).
Expert-recommendation claim needs evidence on file (ASCI-RPT-BPC); whether doctor endorsement is permissible is open Q6 (CCPA-13) - route to legal.

issues.concern: Multi-part efficacy claim (irritation, weakened barrier) needs finished-product data on file (ASCI-1.1).
Keep the HRIPT/clinical test on file; Minimalist states such tests explicitly (brand_corpus §3.5).
SEO scaffolding, not consumer copy.

issues.concern: Claims to clear and prevent acne - treatment/prevention of a skin disorder is drug language (DCA-DRUG-DEF, whose violation example is 'Treats acne and prevents breakouts'; Q1 itself labels 'treats acne' a drug claim).
Recurrence-prevention claim for acne - 'prevention of any disease or disorder' (DCA-DRUG-DEF; ASCI-3.4).
No source/date in the ad (ASCI-1.2; open Q8).
Antibacterial mechanism claim for acne (open Q1/Q2 - route to legal).
Unsubstantiated superlative; ingredient literature is not product proof (CCPA-4 4(1)(f); ASCI-RPT-BPC).
Chemophobic framing Minimalist explicitly rejects ('chemical-free products don't exist', brand_corpus §6, S3); misleading by implication (COS-R36).

issues.phrase: They tackle pimple at the source rather than just clearing surface oil
issues.concern: Treatment-style mechanism talk plus an implied knock at other cleansers (ASCI-4.1 denigration by implication).
Natural/clean halo (ASCI-RPT-BPC); off-brand for Minimalist (brand_corpus §6).

reviewer_note: 'Clears & Prevents Pimples & Acne' plus 'prevents reoccurence' is acne treatment/prevention language a cosmetic cannot carry, beyond the fixable unsourced 'clinically proven' and chemophobic lines.

Absolute 'spotless' promise (ASCI-1.5; ASCI-1.4).
No source/date (ASCI-1.2; open Q8).
Germ/hygiene claim drifts toward antimicrobial territory; keep to cleansing language or hold data (Q2).
